caption_L1: This is a bar chart named Copper consumption of the United States from 2006 to 2019 (in 1,000 metric tons). A linear scale of range 0 to 8,000 can be seen on the x-axis, marked Apparent, unmanufactured**. Along the y-axis, Reported, refined is drawn.
caption_L2L3: In 1760 there was a vast increase in apparent unmanufactured copper. There was a huge drop in 1800 and consumption dropped by a further half in 1810 where it remained at a slow and steady incline until 2140.
